Q: postgresql.conf contains errors A:

I saw this contains errors; unaffected changes in the /var/log file, and found that the actual errors were in the systemd journal. Try journalctl -u postgresql@13-main (adjust for whatever version you're running.

Once you have the actual error log in hand, you should be able to address your configuration issue. In my case, I was binding to an invalid address:

# journalctl -u postgresql@13-main
...
Oct 21 ...: Error: /usr/lib/postgresql/13/bin/pg_ctl /usr/lib/postgresql/13/bin/pg_ctl start -D /var/lib/postgresql/13/main -l /var/log/postgresql/postgresql-13-main.log -s -o  -c config_file="/etc/postgresql/13/main/postgresql.co>
Oct 21 ...: 2022-10-21 18:47:20 UTC LOG:  starting PostgreSQL 13.8 (Ubuntu 13.8-1.pgdg20.04+1) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.1) 9.4.0, 64-bit
Oct 21 ...: 2022-10-21 18:47:20 UTC LOG:  could not bind IPv4 address "172.17.0.1": Cannot assign requested address
Oct 21 ...: 2022-10-21 18:47:20 UTC HINT:  Is another postmaster already running on port 5432? If not, wait a few seconds and retry.
Oct 21 ...: 2022-10-21 18:47:20 UTC WARNING:  could not create listen socket for "172.17.0.1"

Oct 21 ...: pg_ctl: could not start server

Q: Error with loadmat in scipy: could not read bytes A:

For anyone getting a similar error, I fixed mine using the byte_order parameter.

byte_order='native' fixed my problem, but the options are (‘native’, ‘=’, ‘little’, ‘<’, ‘BIG’, ‘>’) (I'm using scypi 1.7.0).

Docs: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.io.loadmat.html

Q: Should I put my statemachine code in its own microservice? A:

Both are acceptable and used in practice. There can be some optimization/savings in the colocation architecture but generally a separate/devoted service for the state machine/orchestrator gains the inherit advantages of ms architecture (decoupling, deployment, scaling, etc.) and in particular is safer as far as future extensibility. hth.

Q: jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBElement and com.sheets.model.generated.SpreadSheet are in unnamed module of loader 'app' A:

having read your suggestion again, I tried not casting at all, and it now works. I also found that I did not need to add @XmlRootElement(name = "SpreadSheet") to the spreadsheet class. Just do not cast.

Many thanks. StuartM

Q: Why is my BigQuery code saying it doesn't recognize a table name? A:

The problem is likely that you need to use the fully qualified table name, just as in the FROM and JOIN clauses.

ON modern-ellipse-438015-c0.Bellabeat.DailyActivity3.Id = modern-ellipse-438015-c0.Bellabeat.DailyActivity4.Id

To avoid having to repeat these long names, I recommend you assign aliases:

FROM modern-ellipse-438015-c0.Bellabeat.DailyActivity3 da3
JOIN modern-ellipse-438015-c0.Bellabeat.DailyActivity4 da4
ON da3.Id = da4.Id

Note also that it's not necessary to enclose the table name in backticks when it contains - characters.

Q: Redis command to get all available keys? A:

Using Python3 - Ubuntu:

Copy and past this shell script in a terminal, e.g. in the home folder:
It'll create a folder $HOME/pyredis and install an environment using venv:
mkdir pyredis; cd pyredis; python3 -m venv ./; source ./bin/activate; pip install redis; touch pyredis.py

Paste the content bellow inside the file pyredis.py:

# pyredis.py
import redis

print('# connecting to Redis server')

r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, db=0)

print('# printing the keys')
for key in r.scan_iter():
    print(key)
print('# all keys printed')

Execute the script:
Enter in the folder, e.g. $HOME/pyredis and type:
python3 pyredis.py
